title: easi.run
intro.1: A real Google Chrome on your own server, for an agent to drive and a person to watch and take over, streamed to your browser.
intro.2: easi.run runs each browser session in its own set of containers and shows it on a web page. The agent works the page; you watch it live, and at any moment you take control, type a password or a 2FA code yourself, and give back. Text of four characters or more you type or paste while you hold control is replaced by [redacted] in what the agent returns to its caller (see Security).
what-a-session-gives.title: What a session gives you
what-a-session-gives.1: The picture and the sound: static content as lossless tiles, motion as AV1 video, sound as Opus.
what-a-session-gives.2: Exact control: only the viewer holding the control lease sends input, and the agent waits while you hold it (see Sessions).
what-a-session-gives.3: Clipboard both ways (text), downloads to your own Downloads folder, and files to the page through its file chooser or by dragging them onto the screen.
what-a-session-gives.4: Recording on the server, with your camera and microphone if you want them, straight to your Downloads (see Sessions).
what-a-session-gives.5: An egress per session: traffic can leave through an upstream proxy you name, with the browser’s time zone and languages set to match.
how-it-fits-together.title: How it fits together
how-it-fits-together.1: Two containers run all the time: the admin, the HTTPS web app and API you open, and the controller, the only holder of the Docker socket, which runs a closed set of operations on fixed templates: it creates, inspects and stops each session’s containers, attaches to, stops and restarts its agent, and removes what an earlier run left. Four more start for each session: the display, a headless Wayland compositor that shows Chrome, encodes its picture and sound and applies input; the browser, Google Chrome; its proxy, the browser’s only way out; and the agent, the Cua Driver, which reads the page through its accessibility tree and its screen, and acts through virtual input. Security says what each may do.
how-it-fits-together.2: To view, use a recent Chrome or Chromium. Start with the Quick start, or try the live demo first.
